title: tracy-host hands teardown its own job and log directories, and teardown keeps the records still running
steps: S1: From the TCH checkout run: node --test --test-reporter=tap apps/tracy-host/test/provision.test.mjs packages/fleet/tracy-fleet-operation/test/teardown-volumes.test.mjs

S2: Record the exit code, the '# tests', '# pass', '# fail' lines and the result of each case whose name starts with: "POST /_host/teardown: teardown.sh is handed the job and log directories this host really uses"; "step 5 drops this site's finished job records and keeps the ones still queued or running".
expect: S1 exits 0 with '# fail 0' and '# pass' equal to '# tests' (at least 70).

Every named case is 'ok' (none 'not ok', none '# SKIP'): POST /_host/teardown runs teardown.sh with JOBS_DIR = the host's jobsDir and HOOK_LOG_DIR = its logDir; step 5 drops only finished records of the label (state not queued or running; no state counts as finished).
evidence: 05/10/2026 local stand: deleting a site left its job records (whole slabs of its content in `output`) and its provision log on the host, and teardown's 'keeping .../teardown-<label>.log' named a file that did not exist: step 5 used the Python hooks' defaults /var/lib/tracy-jobs and /var/log/tracy-hooks, which the tracy-host container does not have. Red cbdc76842 (both cases not ok on 6c43f9c70), fix e0ed33a26.
fence: A teardown's own running record, or a job still queued for the label, is never pruned, so the deploy drain cannot read the host as idle mid-teardown.

tests: POST /_host/teardown: teardown.sh is handed the job and log directories this host really uses
step 5 drops this site's finished job records and keeps the ones still queued or running
